text:
maria: Started a replay run against last week's traffic traces to sanity-check kernel selection sensitivity. Goal: see how batch formation + queue prioritization interacts with kernel fallback when KV warmup lag is simulated.

aj: How are you toggling kernel selection? kernel-heuristic v1/v2?

maria: I baked a small shim in the replayer to force kernel preferences per-model: {fp16-fastmatmul, int8-quantized, fallback-gemm}. Also simulated two KV states: cold (no prefetched KV) and warm (80% hits).

devon: nice. Did you vary token_budget targets? earlier experiments suggested different optima for short vs long seqs.

maria: Yes — swept token_budget = [64,128,256,512]. Batch formation window fixed at 10ms for base runs; also ran 3ms and 25ms for sensitivity.

perf-bot: Replay job 1939991111 started: 12k requests, 4 model variants, 72 combos

leah: Can you paste the latency P95 diffs? even a 5% bump matters.

maria: ```
P95 latencies (ms) - cold KV, window=10ms:
  fp16-fastmatmul: 120 -> 130 (+8%)
  int8-quantized: 140 -> 155 (+11%)
  fallback-gemm: 220 -> 210 (-4%)
Warm KV: fp16 90, int8 95, fallback 200
```

aj: Hmm fallback-gemm better under cold KV? maybe because it's less sensitive to KV miss jitter due to lower memory pressure?

devon: Also check throughput: int8 had higher tokens/sec when token_budget=128 but collapsed at 512 due to kernel thrash - switching kernels mid-request is expensive.

maria: Yes. Observed kernel churn when batchers grew beyond 64 tokens average. Kernel switch cost ~6-12ms per switch measured in profiler.

perf-bot: Profiler snapshot attached: top syscalls: GPU memcpy, kernel init, scheduler lock contention.

maria: I added a cheap heuristic: avoid switching kernel if current batch has >N requests with same target kernel; N=8 reduced churn and P95 by ~6% on the int8 configs.

leah: Does that hurt cost? e.g., keeping a suboptimal kernel longer might increase token/time cost.

maria: Tradeoff: small increase in average token latency for those few batches but net throughput improved; unit-cost estimates show ~3% lower token GPU-seconds due to fewer reinitializations.

aj: What's the recommended token_budget target per workload now?

maria: For our mixed short/long trace, token_budget=128 with window=10ms + kernel-stability N=8 is best. But for latency-critical tail-sensitive workloads prefer 64 and keep kernel-stability strict.

devon: We should feed these configs into A/B harness for a week before rolling. Can the canary route use kernel-stability flag?

maria: Yes canary API accepts config overrides per route. I'll prepare an A/B with ~10k qps split 80/20.

sre-bot: FYI created canary cluster 'replay-scan-1' with capacity ~1200 rps.

leah: Also add KV prefetch probe: simulate 50% warmup delay to mimic cold-start of new prefixes.

maria: Done. Added two arms: prefetch-on and prefetch-off.

perf-bot: A/B run finished: arm A (current baseline) vs arm B (token_budget=128, kernel-stability N=8, prefetch-on). Summary: arm B p95 -6.2%, p99 -3.4%, throughput +4.8%, GPU-seconds per 1M tokens -3.1%.

aj: Nice. Any regression cases? long-seq tails?

maria: Edge case: a small cohort (~2% of requests) with seq_len>4k saw +8% p99 due to longer-serving batches holding kernel-binding and increasing queuing for others. Plan: add a big-request fast-path that caps batch size and forces immediate dispatch.

devon: Sounds good. Also we should add a metric in console: kernel-switch-rate per minute + kv-hit-trajectory.

maria: Agree. I'll add dashboards and an alert if kernel-switch-rate > X.

leah: When do you want to roll to prod?

maria: After one more week of A/B and a smoke on Dedicated. I'll open a rollout PR with config defaults and documentation.

aj: Please include the perf traces and the replayer job spec in the PR.

maria: Will do. Attaching the replayer command:```
./replayer --trace=2026-03-10-traffic --kernels=fp16,int8,fallback --sweep=token_budget:64,128,256,512 --window_ms=3,10,25 --kernel_stability=8
```

perf-bot: Artifacts uploaded: s3://redwood-perf/replays/1939991111/*

maria: :thumbsup: thanks all.
